rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.quote: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.summary: Landlords in San Diego cannot terminate a tenancy without just cause, which includes either at-fault reasons (like non-payment of rent or lease violations) or no-fault reasons (like owner move-in or substantial remodel).
rules.effective_date_evidence: Retitled to "Residential Tenant Protections" on 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.
rules.coverage_text: housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome
rules.exemption_note: Exempts owner-occupied single-family residences with 2 or fewer bedrooms/ADUs/JADUs rented; owner-occupied duplexes; properties where tenant shares bathroom/kitchen with landlord; certain single-family homes and condominiums owned by natural persons; affordable housing; mobilehomes subject to MRL; short-term rentals; and other categories in § 98.0703
rules.penalty: wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times actual economic damages; reasonable attorney's fees and costs; injunctive and equitable relief; punitive damages

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Eviction
rules.quote: Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant's lease in effect at the date of the notice. If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant's lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.summary: Landlords must provide relocation assistance of two months' rent for no-fault evictions, or three months' rent if the tenant is a senior (62+) or disabled, either as a direct payment or rent waiver.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Retitled to "Residential Tenant Protections" on 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.
rules.coverage_text: housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome
rules.exemption_note: Same exemptions as § 98.0704; applies regardless of tenant's income or length of tenancy
rules.penalty: landlord liable for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages

rules.title: Right to Return After No-Fault Eviction
rules.quote: If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant: advised the landlord in writing within 30 days of the termination notice of the tenant's desire to receive an offer to renew the tenancy; and provided the landlord a mailing address or email address for the landlord to send the offer, including any change of mailing address or email address.
rules.summary: Tenants evicted for owner move-in, code compliance, or substantial remodel/demolition have the right to be offered their unit first if it becomes available for rent within five years, provided they requested this in writing within 30 days of the eviction notice.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Retitled to "Residential Tenant Protections" on 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.
rules.coverage_text: housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome
rules.exemption_note: Same exemptions as § 98.0704; only applies to evictions under § 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4)

rules.title: Buyout Agreement Requirements
rules.quote: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.
rules.summary: Buyout agreements between landlords and tenants must exceed the relocation assistance amount the tenant would be entitled to under the law, or the agreement is void.
rules.effective_date_evidence: Retitled to "Residential Tenant Protections" on 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.
rules.coverage_text: housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome
rules.exemption_note: Same exemptions as § 98.0704; includes detailed disclosure and written agreement requirements
rules.penalty: buyout agreements not complying with requirements are void
